description: Exaggerates the spectral (formant) contour of each analysis window. Values below 1 narrow the formants and widen the troughs — an increasingly tight filter focused on the spectral peaks; values above 1 widen the formants — increasingly fuzzy and diffuse, adding noise elements as partials are moved. Operates on PVOC analysis files (.ana).
musical_use: Push a sound toward pitched resonance or toward noise. The manual recommends exaggeration around 0.5 as a balance between original and treated sound; lower values act like ever-tighter bandpass filtering, drawing pitch out of complex material (reminiscent of trace-style thinning at the extreme), while values above 1 diffuse the peaks — around 5 a pitched source picks up a light buzzy sheen, and by 10 a complex source turns distinctly fuzzy and noisy (widening actually moves partials, so noise elements are added, not just softened). Sweeping the value with a breakpoint file travels between the pitched-resonant and noisy states over the course of the file. Also usable on an extracted spectral envelope to reshape its contour.

exaggeration.description: Contour exaggeration factor. < 1 narrows formants and widens troughs (focuses on the peaks; tight-filter effect); > 1 widens formants (diffuses the peaks; fuzzy effect). CDP enforces the range 0.001 to 1000 — negative values are refused despite the banner's wording. May vary over time via a breakpoint file.

examples.description: Manual-recommended balance point between original and treated sound.
examples.expected_use: Bring out pitched resonances within a complex source without losing its identity.

known_issues: Banner-vs-manual divergence: the banner claims 'exaggeration >0 will widen troughs: <0 will widen peaks', but negative values are refused — probed -0.5 yields 'ERROR: Parameter[1] Value (-0.500000) out of range (0.001000 to 1000.000000)'. The HTML manual's reading is the correct one: < 1 widens troughs / narrows formants, > 1 narrows troughs / widens formants.
